title: GTA 6 PC Port Takedown: Why GitHub Pulled 3,007 Repos
desc: No official GTA 6 PC version exists. Take-Two's DMCA notice of November 24, 2026 led GitHub to pull the Leonida PC port network of 3,007 repos. Why it happened.
keywords: gta 6 pc port, gta 6 pc, is gta 6 on pc, does gta 6 run on pc yet, leonida github, project leonida, gta 6 dmca, take-two dmca, gta 6 pc leak, gta 6 github
question: Why did Take-Two take down the GTA 6 PC port on GitHub, and is there an official GTA 6 PC version?
cta: Worried about leaks of your code or data? Have your systems reviewed and hardened.
body:
Short answer. There is no official GTA 6 PC version: on November 26, 2026, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto VI page offered the game only for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The unofficial "PC port" called Leonida is gone because Take-Two sent GitHub a copyright (DMCA) notice, posted on November 24, 2026, and GitHub processed it against the project's entire network of 3,007 repositories.

We read Take-Two's notice in GitHub's public DMCA record, the four other notices Take-Two sent GitHub in November 2026, GitHub's own takedown policy and Rockstar's game page. Below: what the notice says, why one notice removed thousands of copies at once, what can happen next, why "GTA 6 PC download" offers deserve suspicion, and what any business that owns software or content can learn from how fast this moved.

Is there an official GTA 6 PC version?

No, not as of November 26, 2026. Rockstar announced on November 19, 2026 that Grand Theft Auto VI was available, and its Grand Theft Auto VI page lists two platforms: PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. PC is not listed. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date on that page, so any site or video promising a PC download of GTA 6 is not offering something Rockstar sells.

Search interest reflects that gap. In Google Trends for the United States over the seven days to November 26, 2026, related searches for "gta 6 pc" included "leonida github" and "gta 6 pc port tracker" as Breakout terms and "does gta 6 run on pc yet" up 1,200%.

What Take-Two's DMCA notice says

The notice comes from "the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games." It asked GitHub to remove one developer's repository "and the 2900+ forks attached to it," which it said infringe Take-Two's copyright in Grand Theft Auto VI.

The repository described itself as "a native PC recompilation of the Xbox version of Grand Theft Auto 6." Take-Two made three arguments:

  • Copyright. The repository "reproduces copyrighted expression in GRAND THEFT AUTO VI and is a derivative work" of the game.
  • Terms of service. It "exceeds the license Rockstar Games grants to users" and breaks at least Section 2.3 of Rockstar's terms, which, as quoted in the notice, bars players from copying, decompiling, reverse engineering or creating derivative works.
  • Timing. "On November 20, 2026, stolen game files from an Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI were publicly distributed. The following day, this Leonida repository opened." Its instructions required Xbox Series game files as input.

The project did not ship the game files itself; it told users to bring their own. Take-Two called that instruction "intentionally misleading," arguing that, given the timing, the files users were expected to supply were the leaked ones. Decrypt, which reported the notice on November 25, 2026, wrote that the project's page had disappeared on Monday, November 23, showing an error page rather than a DMCA notice.

Why GitHub removed 3,007 repositories at once

On GitHub, a fork is a copy of someone else's repository in another user's account. GitHub's DMCA takedown policy says it "will not automatically disable forks when disabling a parent repository," because, in its words, forks "belong to different users, may have been altered in significant ways," and GitHub "does not conduct any independent investigation into forks." It expects the copyright owner to name the forks.

The policy has one exception for large networks. If a network holds more than 100 repositories, GitHub "may consider disabling the entire network" when the notice states that, based on a representative sample, "all or most of the forks are infringing to the same extent as the parent repository." Take-Two's notice did that. GitHub's note at the top of the record says it "processed the takedown notice against the entire network of 3,007 repositories."

So the 3,007 figure is GitHub's count of the whole network, and the "2900+" figure is Take-Two's count of forks in its request. Both come from the same record.

The four GTA V notices that came first

Leonida was not Take-Two's only GitHub notice that month. As of November 26, 2026, GitHub's November 2026 DMCA folder held five Take-Two notices. The four dated November 18, 2026 all concern Grand Theft Auto V, not GTA VI: projects that tried to run GTA V on iPhone and Mac, on Android, in a web browser, and through a WebAssembly runtime.

The three GTA V notices that give a number name 626 forks between them. In each of the five, the project ran Rockstar's game somewhere Rockstar does not sell it. Muguet and Leonida both told users to supply their own game files, and four of the five notices named forks.

Can the takedown be reversed?

Under GitHub's policy, a developer whose repository was disabled can send a counter notice. If the copyright owner then wants the content kept down, it has to go to court: GitHub says that if it does not receive a copy of a lawsuit "within 10-14 days," it "will re-enable the disabled content."

Decrypt also reported that the project's Discord server was removed for copyright reasons and that the developer later posted that he was no longer working on the project. We have not seen those posts ourselves. This is general information about GitHub's process, not legal advice.

Why "GTA 6 PC download" offers are risky

As of November 26, 2026, the official game is on two consoles only, and Leonida, which Decrypt called one of the most prominent projects trying to port the leaked Xbox build, has been removed. In our view, a GTA 6 PC download offered anywhere is therefore either built from leaked files or not the real game. We would treat it as unsafe: it may break Rockstar's terms, and an installer from an unknown source can carry anything.

The same caution applies to "early access" and "beta key" offers, which we covered in our guide to GTA 6 early access scams.

The business lesson: speed and a public record

Take-Two is the parent company of Rockstar Games (see who owns GTA 6), and its response shows how a rights owner works when its product leaks. According to the notice, the stolen files were distributed on November 20, 2026; the notice in GitHub's record is dated four days later. It named the forks explicitly, used the large-network wording that GitHub's policy asks for, and quoted the clause of Rockstar's terms it said the project broke.

The same tools exist for anyone whose code, designs or content get copied: a platform's published takedown process, terms of service that spell out what users may not do, and someone watching where copies appear. faqs: Is there a GTA 6 PC version?
No official one as of November 26, 2026. Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto VI page offers the game for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and it gives no PC release date.
Why was the GTA 6 PC port taken down?

Take-Two sent GitHub a DMCA notice, posted on November 24, 2026, saying the Leonida project reproduced copyrighted parts of GTA VI, was a derivative work, broke Section 2.3 of Rockstar's terms, and required Xbox Series files, which Take-Two linked to a stolen build distributed on November 20, 2026.

An unofficial GitHub project that described itself as a native PC recompilation of the Xbox version of GTA 6. It did not include the game files; its instructions asked users to supply Xbox Series files.
How many repositories did GitHub take down?
GitHub says it processed Take-Two's notice against the entire network of 3,007 repositories. Take-Two's notice itself described one repository and more than 2,900 forks.
Did Take-Two send other DMCA notices in November 2026?
Yes. GitHub's record holds four more Take-Two notices dated November 18, 2026, all about Grand Theft Auto V ports for iPhone and Mac, Android, web browsers and a WebAssembly runtime.
Can a GitHub DMCA takedown be reversed?

Possibly. Under GitHub's policy, a counter notice can lead GitHub to restore the content unless the copyright owner sends a copy of a filed lawsuit within 10 to 14 days. Get legal advice before filing one; this is general information, not legal advice.
